s1.syndrome_frame: intermittent right pelvic pain and gross hematuria with a ureteral mass
salient_findings: tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
key_facts: renal ultrasound and cystoscopy showed no abnormalities
intravenous urography demonstrated a tubular filling defect
retrograde ureteropyelography confirmed a 5 cm long tubular mass
flexible ureteroscopy revealed a pedunculated ureteral tumor
urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy were negative for malignancy
staging CT scan showed slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis and subtle thickening of the right ureter

shortlist.label: Ureteral fibroepithelial polyp
shortlist.why_kept: Pedunculated ureteral tumor with a vulnerable surface and negative biopsy for malignancy

shortlist.label: Upper urinary tract urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Gross hematuria and ureteral mass, although biopsy was negative for malignancy

shortlist.label: Ureteral leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ureteral mass and negative biopsy for malignancy, with leiomyoma being a possible benign cause

shortlist.label: Ureteral endometrioma
shortlist.why_kept: Ureteral mass and pelvic pain, with endometrioma being a possible cause in rare cases

shortlist.label: Inverted papilloma of the ureter
shortlist.why_kept: Ureteral mass and negative biopsy for malignancy, with inverted papilloma being a rare benign tumor

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of gross hematuria and intermittent right pelvic pain, combined with imaging findings of a tubular filling defect and a pedunculated ureteral tumor, are consistent with a ureteral fibroepithelial polyp. The negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy for malignancy also support this diagnosis.

rejected.why: Not typically associated with the patient's symptoms and imaging findings
